answer: One concrete defense is a refundable stake each agent must lock before acting, slashed when peers prove misbehavior. Like timber that must be seasoned before it bears weight, a stake aged through a waiting period proves the agent paid time as well as money. A ferrous deposit cannot be copied cheaply, so every fake identity costs real funds, and a prism of independent checks - reputation, activity history, and peer attestation - splits each claim into many verifiable signals. An attacker must fund and age each identity separately, so sybils grow expensive while verification stays cheap.
